project: Evaluation of Advanced Decoding Strategies on Model B Logits
methodology: We execute six different decoding algorithms on the same identical logits tensor extracted from Abdul Basit's Mujawwad and Mishary Alafasy's Murattal recitations of Surah 67, Ayah 1.

strategy_a_standard_ctc.name: Standard CTC Forced Alignment (Viterbi Trellis)
strategy_a_standard_ctc.description: Standard backtracking without state-transition weights or duration constraints.
strategy_a_standard_ctc.vulnerability: Extremely sensitive to blank emissions. If the model decays into blanks during a sustained Madd, standard Viterbi immediately collapses the path, creating premature word boundaries.

strategy_b_duration_aware.name: CTC Alignment with Duration-Aware Transition Penalties
strategy_b_duration_aware.description: Adds a log-penalty multiplier for staying in the same character state too long, or moving to the next character state too early, proportional to known Arabic syllabic rates.
strategy_b_duration_aware.vulnerability: Slightly improves Mujawwad by forcing the Alif state to remain open longer, but causes slight degradation on fast Hadr recitations by over-penalizing rapid natural transitions.

strategy_c_repetition_handling.name: CTC Alignment with Controlled Token Repetition Handling
strategy_c_repetition_handling.description: Adjusts the self-loop probability in the trellis to penalize long sequences of repeated character tokens, pushing the model to transit to subsequent graphemes.
strategy_c_repetition_handling.vulnerability: Causes severe skipping on words with naturally doubled Arabic characters (Shaddah), such as 'ٱلَّذِى' and 'كُلِّ', leading to premature boundaries.

strategy_d_blank_aware.name: CTC Alignment with Blank-Aware Transition Handling
strategy_d_blank_aware.description: Applies a dynamic damping factor to [PAD] token transitions when inside a continuous vowel segment, distributing the blank frames proportionally to neighboring vowels.
strategy_d_blank_aware.vulnerability: Helps bridge small gaps of silence or blank frames, but fails when the blank-lock is longer than 1.0s because there are no adjacent high-confidence vowel frames to latch onto.

strategy_e_ayah_level_constraints.name: CTC Alignment with Ayah-Level Constraints
strategy_e_ayah_level_constraints.description: Prunes the search space by locking the trellis starting frames and ending frames to the active Ayah audio segment boundaries derived from an initial coarse VAD pass.
strategy_e_ayah_level_constraints.vulnerability: Significantly improves both Murattal and Mujawwad by preventing the trellis from drifting into leading or trailing silences, but cannot solve internal word-boundary distortion caused by acoustic-emission collapses.

strategy_f_word_level_constraints.name: CTC Alignment with Word-Level Constraints
strategy_f_word_level_constraints.description: Imposes local maximum and minimum duration limits on individual word spans based on linguistic statistics of Classical Arabic phonology.
strategy_f_word_level_constraints.vulnerability: Yields the absolute best numerical scores of all strategies by restricting the word lengths mathematically. However, it is an analytical boundary constraint (essentially forcing a proportional duration limit), which behaves less like an acoustic detector and more like an automated guesser.

scientific_verdict: While advanced decoding strategies (such as word-level and ayah-level constraints) can substantially cushion alignment errors and prevent extreme drift, THEY CANNOT FIX the underlying issue of missing acoustic information. No CTC decoding algorithm can extract speech boundaries from a sequence of logits that consists entirely of blank ([PAD]) predictions.
